source: Xiong et al. (2025) How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents (addition strategies)
finding: Adding every run to memory hurt on all four agents. A frozen small memory often beat coarse-judged growth. Only a strict (ground-truth) filter beat the frozen bank on all four.
quote: noisy or low-quality additions can harm memory utility
limits: Single run per cell, no variance. The strict judge uses ground truth, which a live agent rarely has. Not a case-field ablation.
agent_relevance: Outcome label quality gates the value of S9. Default to a small verified bank; do not write unverified runs as cases.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) error propagation and experience-following
finding: Stored wrong outputs get copied: output similarity rises with input similarity (experience-following). Against an error-free retrieval variant, add-all and coarse selection open a gap that grows over time.
numbers: Figure 4: the gap to the ground-truth-output variant is immediate and widens for add-all and coarse addition (RegAgent, AgentDriver). With strict addition AgentDriver closes the gap and passes it after about 2000 executions. Input/output similarity correlation near 1 for RegAgent under addition. The fixed-memory arm showed lower similarity and high performance.
quote: high input similarity often correlates with high output similarity
limits: Synthetic RegAgent exaggerates copying. GPT-4o-mini family backbones; GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 only in appendix pattern checks.
agent_relevance: Experience-following is measured and real. A near-duplicate wrong case is the most dangerous. Require a verified outcome before the agent may copy a case.

source: Xiong et al. (2025) memory deletion, capacity cap, distribution shift
finding: Utility-based deletion (drop records whose later retrievals led to poor results) helped with a strict evaluator and was unstable with untuned coarse judges. A fixed cap with a combined rule still beat the frozen bank.
numbers: Strict addition, EHRAgent/AgentDriver/CIC-IoT: no deletion 38.67/51.00/85.40 at sizes 1012/1178/904; history-based 42.06/51.81/89.60 at 784/846/788; combined 42.34/49.97/85.50 at 248/323/188. With the untuned GPT-4o-mini history judge deletion gained on EHRAgent and lost on AgentDriver. Caps tested: 100 (EHR) and 180 (AgentDriver).
limits: Table 2 text is partly garbled; value-to-row pairing read from column order. EHRAgent no-deletion strict is 38.67 here and 38.50 in Table 1. Four agents, one run each, horizons about 1 to 4k tasks.
agent_relevance: A per-case utility count (retrievals then outcomes) works as an eviction rule only when outcomes are trustworthy. Banks beyond a few thousand are untested.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank, simulated judge accuracy
finding: Success on WebArena Shopping barely moved when labels that decide which memories are written were flipped 10 to 50 percent of the time.
numbers: Gemini-2.5-flash, Shopping subset. Real judge accuracy 72.7 percent. Simulated accuracy 100 down to 50 percent gave success from about 50.6 down to about 47.6, all above the 39.0 no-memory baseline. One run per point.
quote: judge's accuracy does not significantly impact the performance
limits: Gaps of 1 to 3 points are within plausible run noise. Even random labels (50 percent) beat no memory, so much of the gain comes from strategy text rather than correct labels. Values read from a plot.
agent_relevance: Strategy-style records tolerate label noise on web tasks. This conflicts with d01 where raw trajectories used as demos did not. Record format may decide noise tolerance.

source: Ouyang et al. (2025/2026) ReasoningBank, three backbones
finding: Memory gain did not grow with model strength. Gains over no memory: Gemini-2.5-flash +8.3, Gemini-2.5-pro +7.2, Claude-3.7-sonnet +4.6 overall on WebArena.
numbers: WebArena overall: flash 40.5 no memory, 48.8 ReasoningBank, 51.8 with MaTTS; pro 46.7, 53.9, 56.3; Claude-3.7 41.7, 46.3, 48.8. AWM: pro 47.6 (+0.9), Claude 40.8 (-0.9). Synapse: pro 47.7, Claude 42.6. Reported standard errors about 7 to 9 points per cell.
quote: improves the overall success rate on WebArena by +8.3, +7.2, and +4.6
limits: Standard errors are large on small subsets, so the Claude gain is not clearly above noise. No model smaller than flash.
agent_relevance: Memory gains shrink on stronger backbones. A weaker-form memory (AWM) can sit at or below baseline on a strong model.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Agentic Context Engineering, injected harmful reflections
finding: A harmful reflector forced to inject bad or conflicting playbook items every X steps left accuracy above the base model unless corruption hit every step.
numbers: FiNER, DeepSeek-V3.1 generator. Base 70.7. No harmful updates 78.3. Harmful every 100 steps 78.2; 50: 78.2; 25: 77.8; 10: 77.0; 5: 76.1; every step: 66.7 (-4.0 vs base). Reflector strength: GPT-OSS-120B 76.6, DeepSeek 78.3, GPT-5.1 78.5.
quote: performance drops below the base model only under sustained adversarial corruption
limits: One benchmark, one run per row, no variance. Bad items are adversarial, not natural mistakes. Items are merged and deduplicated, which dilutes bad ones.
agent_relevance: Best dose-response found for noise. One bad update in five cost about 2 points; all bad updates were worse than no memory. Keep a merge and dedupe step.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Agentic Context Engineering, context collapse and missing feedback
finding: Rewriting the whole memory each step made it collapse. Without ground-truth or execution signals, both ACE and Dynamic Cheatsheet could fall below baseline.
numbers: AppWorld: a context of 18,282 tokens at accuracy 66.7 collapsed to 122 tokens at 57.1, below the 63.7 no-adaptation baseline. Incremental delta updates avoid this. With execution feedback but no labels ACE still gained +14.8 on average on AppWorld. On the finance set without reliable labels some cells fell.
quote: constructed context can be polluted by spurious or misleading signals
limits: Authors' own method. Collapse shown on one Dynamic Cheatsheet trace.
agent_relevance: Store cases append-only with small edits, never full rewrites. Execution results are enough signal on code tasks; on QA without a verifier memory may hurt.

source: Dong et al. (2025) MINJA memory injection (NeurIPS 2025)
finding: Ordinary users can plant misleading records using queries only. Agents retrieve and follow them. This is a direct measure of experience-following with GPT-4 and GPT-4o.
numbers: Injection success above 95 percent overall. Attack success above 70 percent in half the configurations and above 90 percent for GPT-4 EHR on eICU and GPT-4o RAP on WebShop. With 5 demos only about 3.2 benign examples were retrieved per test query; adding more benign records lowered utility drop and attack impact. Nine victim-target pairs.
quote: the malicious records retrieved for demonstration may mislead the agent
limits: Adversarial, not ordinary errors. Older agents (EHRAgent, RAP, MMLU QA). No current frontier model.
agent_relevance: A misleading case is followed even by GPT-4-class models. Dense correct neighbours and provenance checks are mitigations. Untested on current frontier models.

finding: Poisoning under 0.1 percent of memory or knowledge-base entries gave about 80 percent attack success with about 1 percent or less loss of normal performance.
numbers: Autonomous driving, knowledge QA and healthcare EHR agents. Average attack success about 80 percent or more; benign drop about 1 percent or less; poison rate below 0.1 percent.
quote: average attack success rate of 80% with minimal impact on benign performance
limits: Backdoor trigger with white-box embedder access: a worst case. Abstract and intro read; not every table.
agent_relevance: Retrieval keys can be steered. A tiny share of bad cases can dominate when the trigger matches. Do not accept cases from unverified sources.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp, procedural memory granularity
finding: Storing both the raw trajectory and a distilled script beat either alone on ALFWorld and on most TravelPlanner scores. Script-only generalised better to new tasks; trajectory-only did better on tasks like seen ones.
quote: trajectories ... better suited for scenarios involving tasks similar to those already completed
limits: Memories built from training trajectories with benchmark reward; one run per cell; ALFWorld templates repeat. On Claude TravelPlanner the combined record is not better than trajectory alone.
agent_relevance: Partly closes gap 2 for repeated-template tasks: keep the concrete case and a short distilled lesson in one S9 record.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp, retrieval key and number retrieved
finding: On TravelPlanner the retrieval key mattered less than having memory at all. Random memories gave most of the gain; query-embedding and keyword-averaged keys added 1 to 4 points.
numbers: Commonsense score. GPT-4o: none 71.93, random 74.59, query key 73.38, AveFact key 76.02. Claude-3.5: 63.49, 63.99, 64.93, 65.76. Qwen2.5-72B: 56.57, 59.76, 61.71, 63.41. On ALFWorld GPT-4o performance rose with number retrieved, plateaued, then fell with too many.
quote: retrieving too many memories can lead to a decline in the agent's performance
limits: One benchmark, one run. Random beat the query key for GPT-4o, so differences are small. Only two key types; no cross-domain test.
agent_relevance: A cheap key (task wording) is nearly as good here. Cap the number of retrieved cases.

source: Fang et al. (2025) Memp, transfer to a smaller model and update rule
finding: Memory written by GPT-4o helped Qwen2.5-14B. Revising memory after a failed use beat plain append.
numbers: Qwen2.5-14B on TravelPlanner with GPT-4o memory: task completion up 5 percent, average steps down 1.6; similar gains on ALFWorld. Reflexion-style update was best, ahead of the next strategy by 0.7 reward points and 14 steps at the last group.
quote: procedural memory ... transferred to a smaller model
limits: Figure values partly garbled. One smaller model, two benchmarks, one run.
agent_relevance: A strong model can write S9 records a weaker model can use. Revise a case after a failed reuse instead of only appending.

finding: Memory gain tracks how alike tasks are inside a dataset. Recurring-structure sets (PDDL, ALFWorld) gain most; AIME-25 and GPQA gain little. Smaller models benefit most.
numbers: Pearson r between within-dataset task similarity and ReMem gain over history: 0.717 (Gemini-2.5-flash), 0.563 (Claude-3.7-sonnet). ReMem steps on ALFWorld 22.6 to 11.5. Simple raw-experience retrieval (ExpRecent, ExpRAG) stayed competitive with AWM and Dynamic Cheatsheet. With unfiltered failures stored, baselines degraded while ReMem held.
quote: recurring task structures facilitate memory reuse and generalization
limits: Table cells are garbled in the PDF text; only figures stated in prose are used. ReMem is the authors' own method.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence for gap 8: puzzle-like sets with little repeat gain little. Do not expect S9 to help on ARC unless tasks share structure.

source: Tang et al. (2025) Agent KB, ablations and store size
finding: Refining a retrieved workflow before use mattered most: raw workflow replay lost 3 points against refined. Small stores (100 examples) already worked; 500 helped more on code.
numbers: GAIA, smolagents + GPT-4.1, pass@1: baseline 55.15; with Agent KB 61.21; without Refine 55.15; without Retrieve 57.58; raw workflow 58.18; without Reason 60.00. Pass@3 55.2 to 73.9. Hand-crafted vs automatic experiences: GAIA 76.97 vs 75.15, SWE-bench Lite 55.67 vs 51.00. Hybrid BM25 + embedding beat either alone. Utility-based eviction is described, not ablated.
quote: retrieved workflows must be adapted rather than replayed
limits: Pass@3 gains may include extra passes; baseline retry parity unclear. Size curve only to 500 in the plot. Single runs.
agent_relevance: Adapt a retrieved case to the new problem before use. Hybrid lexical plus semantic retrieval is a safe default.

finding: An experience library learned from 100 samples lifted a 671B model on AIME, helped 32B and 72B models a little, and hurt a 32B reasoning model on web QA. Unchecked model-written experiences slightly hurt.
numbers: DeepSeek-V3.1-Terminus Mean@32 AIME24/25: ReAct 80.0/67.9; directly generated experiences 79.8/67.3; no ground truth 80.7/68.9; no group comparison 80.4/69.3; full 82.7/73.3. Qwen3-32B 29.1/19.5 to 33.5/25.4; Qwen2.5-72B 13.5/9.6 to 14.9/11.4. QwQ-32B on WebWalkerQA 27.5 to 25.5 pass@1. 51-item WebWalkerQA ablation: ReAct 66.7 pass@1 and 78.4 pass@3 only with experiences.
quote: model capability is a prerequisite for effective experience-based optimization
limits: AIME gains of 1 to 3 points on 30 problems per year are small. Authors' own method. Mean@32 reduces sampling noise.
agent_relevance: Partly closes gap 9: benefit is not monotone in size, and weak reasoners can lose. Also shows small gains on non-repeating puzzles (AIME).

source: Liu et al. (2025) Contextual Experience Replay (CER)
finding: Two kinds of stored experience (page dynamics, skills) both mattered. Learning from successes only was slightly better than successes plus failures. Sampling and memory were complementary.
numbers: WebArena Forum: CER 37.7; without skills 33.3; without dynamics 35.1. Whole WebArena: CER 31.4, success-only 33.5, ReAct baseline 24.3. Forum: sampling and rerank alone 43.1; CER alone 37.7; both 52.6. Llama-3.1-70B on Gitlab: +26.5 percent relative, less than for GPT-4o.
quote: failed trajectories provide some misleading action sequences
limits: One run per row. WebArena templates repeat up to five times. Sampling used more tokens than CER alone, so this is not an equal-token test.
agent_relevance: On one benchmark sampling alone beat memory alone, and combining beat both. For gap 3: complementary, not a substitute. Content-type ablation, not case-field ablation.

source: Zou et al. (2026) DeMem rate-distortion memory, corrupted feedback
finding: A decision-focused conversational memory degraded smoothly when 10 or 20 percent of its binary feedback labels were flipped.
numbers: LoCoMo overall: 91.1 at 0 percent noise, 90.2 at 10, 88.9 at 20; baselines Mnemis 88.8, RAG 63.7. Split precision 85.0, 80.8, 77.6.
limits: Conversational QA memory, not case-based agent memory. Authors' own method. Single run.
agent_relevance: Weak support that moderate label noise is tolerable. Not a case-memory test.
